title: Gelatin Methacryloyl Granular Hydrogel Scaffolds: High-throughput Microgel Fabrication, Lyophilization, Chemical Assembly, and 3D Bioprinting
protocol: Add 200 mL of Dulbecco's phosphate buffered saline (DPBS, 1x) to an Erlenmeyer flask and heat the solution until it reaches 50 °C.
Cover the flask with aluminum foil to prevent evaporation.
Add 20 g of gelatin powder to the DPBS solution at 50 °C while stirring at 240 rpm until the powder is completely dissolved.

Add 16, 2.5, or 0.5 mL of methacrylate anhydride (MA) to the gelatin solution dropwise via a glass Pasteur pipette to synthesize GelMA with a high, medium, or low degree of methacryloyl substitution, respectively.
After 2 h, add 400 mL of DPBS at 50 °C to stop the reaction.
Allow stirring to continue at 50 °C for 10 min.
Pour the solution into a dialysis membrane tubing with 12-14 kDa molecular weight cutoff.
Place the tubing in a 5 L beaker filled with 40 °C ultrapure water.
Stir the water at 240 rpm and 40 °C.
Dialyze the solution against ultrapure water for 10 days and change the water 2x a day to remove unreacted methacrylate anhydride, byproducts, and other impurities.
Add 400 mL of ultrapure water at 40 °C to the GelMA solution.
Stir the mixture at 240 rpm for 15 min.
Filter the solution twice using coffee filters.
Vacuum filter the solution through a 0.2 µm unit.
Pour 25 mL of filtered solution into 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Freeze the tubes horizontally at -80 °C.
Remove caps from frozen tubes after 2 days.
Cover the open tubes with laboratory wipes.
Secure wipes tightly using tape or rubber bands.
Lyophilize the frozen GelMA solution to yield white solid.
Add 30 mg of gelatin powder in 1 mL D2O for control.
Maintain sample at 37 °C until gelatin dissolves completely.
Add 30 mg of lyophilized GelMA in 1 mL D2O for sample.
Maintain this sample at 37 °C until it dissolves completely.
Obtain the 1H NMR spectra of both samples.
Integrate aromatic acids and lysine methylene proton peaks.
Use aromatic acids peak as a reference for degree calculation.
Determine DS using equation (Area of lysine methylene in GelMA / Area of lysine methylene in gelatin) × 100.
Thaw KMPR 1025 and 1035 overnight, avoiding light exposure.
Add KMPR 1025 directly to the middle of the wafer to form an approximately 5 cm circle of photoresist.
Run the spin coater at 3,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Soft bake on a 100 °C hotplate for 12 minutes.
Cool down on the cooling plate for 5 minutes.
Attach the first layer mask to the blank soda lime.
Expose the coated wafer to UV light using a mask aligner for 645 mJ/cm² dosage.
Post bake for 3 min on a 100 °C hotplate.
Cool down on the cooling plate for 5 min.
Spin coat the second layer on the wafer using KMPR 1035 at 1,000 rpm for 30 s.
Soft bake for 30 min on a 100 °C hotplate.
Cool down on the cooling plate for 5 min.
Attach the second layer mask to the blank soda lime and align it using the aligner through standard alignment signs.
Expose to UV light using a mask aligner up to 2,000 mJ/cm².
Post bake for 5 min on a 100 °C hotplate.
Develop for >6 min in SU-8 developer.
Spray with isopropanol.
Thoroughly dry the wafer using nitrogen (N₂) gas.
Pour 50 g of PDMS base part into a transparent plastic cup.
Add 5 g of crosslinker to the plastic cup.
Mix the base and crosslinker vigorously until a creamy texture is obtained.
Vacuum degas the mixture in a desiccator for 20 min until it becomes clear.
Pour the mixture onto the master mold, which is placed inside and taped to a Petri dish.
Put the Petri dish into the desiccator.
Vacuum degas the PDMS mixture for 20 minutes until all bubbles are removed.
Place the Petri dish in a 70°C oven for 2 hours until the PDMS is crosslinked.
Take the Petri dish out of the oven and allow it to cool down.
Cut the devices out of the mold using a scalpel.
Detach the devices slowly from the master mold.
Use the biopsy punch (1.5 mm diameter) to cut holes through the inlets and the outlet.
Remove any dust from the PDMS devices and the glass slides using masking tape.
Place the glass slides and the devices in a plasma cleaner chamber.
Perform the plasma treatment for 45 seconds with air pressure under 400 mTorr.
Remove the slides and devices from the chamber.
Put the device on the glass slide and apply slight pressure.
Put the device in the 70°C oven for 30 minutes to enhance the bonding.
Prepare trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorooctyl)silane (F-silane) solution at 2% v/v in the engineered fluid.
Inject the F-silane solution through the outlet to ensure all devices are exposed.
Wait for 5-10 minutes.
Aspirate the F-silane solution out of the device through the aqueous solution inlet.
Wash the device twice using the engineering fluid and aspirate again.
Place the device in the 70°C oven for 30 minutes to evaporate the remaining oil.
Add 10 mg of lithium phenyl-2,4,6-trimethylbenzoylphosphinate (LAP) to 10 mL of DPBS to prepare a photoinitiator (PI) solution (0.1% w/v).
Wrap the PI solution in aluminum foil to protect it from light.
Dissolve the desired amount of GelMA in the PI solution and place it in the 37 °C oven for 1 hour until a clear solution is obtained.
Wrap the GelMA solution in aluminum foil to protect it from light.
Make a 2% v/v biocompatible surfactant solution in the engineering fluid.
Insert Tygon tubing into the inlets and outlet of the PDMS device.
Insert a 25 G blunt needle at the other end of the Tygon tubing for the inlets.
Place the device under the microscope.
Keep the environment warm (~40 °C) using a hair dryer or space heater.
Load the aqueous and oil solutions into separate syringes, connected to the device.
Start the syringe pumps with flow rates of 160 and 80 µL/min for the oil and aqueous phases, respectively.
Start the oil phase first; ensure the oil fills the channel before starting the aqueous phase.
Collect the droplets in a container and evaluate them via optical microscopy imaging.
Place the collected droplets at 4 °C overnight while protecting them from light to initiate GelMA HMP physical crosslinking and convert the droplets to stable microgels.
Collect physically crosslinked HMPs in thermally durable microcentrifuge tubes or cryovials.
Seal tube caps with a laboratory wipe and tape.
Deep-freeze the physically crosslinked HMPs in liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) for 10 min.
Transfer flash-frozen tubes to a freeze-dryer instrument.
Lyophilize the tubes at low pressure (e.g., 0.06 mbar) for at least 6 h.
Break the pressure slowly after lyophilization cycle is finished.
Add 1 mL of cooled PI solution (0.1% w/v, 4 °C) to the powder to make microgel suspensions.
Vortex the suspension for 5 s.
Centrifuge the suspension at 3,000 × g for 15 s.
Discard the supernatant.
Transfer packed microgel suspension to a mold using a positive displacement pipette.
Expose the suspension to UV light at 400 nm wavelength with an intensity of 15 mW/cm2 for 60 s.
Add 400 µL of 1H,1H-perfluoro-1-octanol (PFO) solution in the engineering fluid (20% v/v) to the physically crosslinked GelMA HMPs.
Vortex for 5 s and centrifuge for 15 s at 300 × g.
Remove the oil phase from the GelMA HMPs via pipetting.
Add 400 µL of PI solution (0.1% w/v) at 4 °C to the microgel suspension.
Vortex for 5 s and centrifuge at 300 × g for 15 s.
Discard the oil afterward.
Repeat the previous step but centrifuge at 3,000 × g.
Remove the supernatant of packed GelMA HMPs via pipetting.
Transfer the packed GelMA HMPs to a mold using a positive displacement pipette.
Expose to UV light (wavelength = 400 nm, intensity = 15 mW/cm2, exposure time = 60 s).
Add 100 mg of nanoplatelet powder to 3 mL of 4 °C ultrapure water to form a nanoparticle dispersion (3.33% w/v).
Vortex the dispersion vigorously inside a 4 °C fridge for 15 min to exfoliate the otherwise aggregated nanoparticles.
Dissolve 50 mg of LAP in 5 mL of 4°C ultrapure water.
Add 333 µL of PI solution (1% w/v) to the exfoliated nanoparticle dispersion.
Wrap the mixture in aluminum foil to protect against ambient light.
Vortex for 1 min to mix the nanoparticle dispersion and PI.
Mix PFO 20% v/v in engineering fluid with GelMA HMPs at a 1:1 volume ratio.
Vortex thoroughly for 5 s.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 15 s and discard the oil phase containing the surfactant.
Add the LAP-supplemented nanoparticle dispersion (4°C) to the washed GelMA HMPs.
Vortex for 15 s, centrifuge at 3,000 × g for 15 s, and discard the remaining oil and supernatant dispersion.
Store the suspension at 4°C while protecting it from light using aluminum foil for 1 day.
Load the NGB into a 3 mL syringe.
Seal the loaded syringe with a cap and parafilm.
Pulse centrifuge at 200 × g to remove trapped air.
Transfer the bioink to a 3 mL cartridge using a female-female Luer-Lok connector.
Centrifuge the cartridge briefly at 200 × g again to remove trapped air.
Keep the NGB at 4°C in a fridge before using.
Prepare a concentrated cell suspension containing ~24 million NIH/3T3 murine fibroblast cells in 100 µL of cell culture medium.
Load the cell suspension into a 3 mL syringe.
Couple the NGB-loaded syringe with the cell-loaded syringe using a female-female Luer-Lok connector.
Mix the cells and NGB gently by pushing back and forth 40 times.
Select the substrate and nozzle type (pneumatic 3 mL syringe equipped with standard conical nozzle).
Calibrate the bioprinter according to device guidelines.
Load the nozzle into the 3 mL printhead.
Optimize printing parameters such as speed and back pressure prior to printing.
Maintain all materials and devices under a biological safety cabinet during cell-laden bioprinting.
Print the NGB or cell-laden NGB using a proper bioprinter with a standard conical nozzle, keeping the printing bed temperature below 10 °C.
Expose the construct to UV light for photocrosslinking (wavelength = 400 nm, intensity = 15 mW/cm2, exposure time = 60 s).
Add PFO (20% v/v in engineering fluid) to the GelMA microgel-oil emulsion at a 1:1 volumetric ratio.
Vortex and centrifuge the mixture at 300 × g for 15 s.
Add PI solution (LAP 0.1% w/v in DPBS) to the GelMA HMPs.
Vortex and centrifuge the mixture at 3,000 × g for 15 s to fabricate GelMA GHS.
Add PI solution (LAP 0.1% w/v in ultrapure water) and nanoplatelet dispersion (3% w/v in ultrapure water) to the GelMA HMP suspension.
Vortex and centrifuge the mixture at 3,000 × g for 15 s to prepare NGB.
